safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 5.0 to 2.87 days; replace with explicit safety stock of 1516 units

narrative: Material PL1__M8AEE259 exhibits high daily demand variability (CV=0.84) with a statistically significant upward trend over the observation period, suggesting growing consumption. Approximately 60% of working days carry positive demand, classifying this as a mixed/variable regime. Lead times average 2.69 days with moderate variability (CV=0.40). The EOQ-based (r,Q) continuous-review policy was selected to minimize total ordering and holding costs, establishing an explicit safety stock of 1,516 units calibrated to a 95% service level, replacing the current SAP approach of zero safety stock and frequent small orders at MOQ.
warnings: 2 demand outliers winsorised at upper bound 1728.92 units
SAP safety stock is 0 — material is currently exposed to stockout risk
Upward demand trend detected (p=0.0005) — reorder point should be reviewed quarterly

research_insights.selection_rationale: With moderately frequent demand (60% non-zero days), significant annual volume (~137K units), and moderate lead-time variability, the classical (r,Q) model with EOQ-derived batch size minimises total inventory cost. The policy is tractable, well-understood by planners, and directly addresses the extreme over-ordering inefficiency in the current SAP setup.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (160,800 units) is not binding — SS+Q = 47,983 units represents only 30% utilisation. No capacity-driven reduction required.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (559) + safety stock (1,516) = 2,075 units is well within max_storage_units (160,800). No infeasibility.
